notes: The San Francisco Call's weekly Real Estate and Financial Section for the whole of 1911, read page by page: every Saturday's section page and its continuation, 96 OCR pages over 51 Saturdays. 1911 is after the 1909 renumbering, so the section prints today's numbers; the pre-1910 guard does not apply, and every entry carries extra.record_date. Taken: numbered addresses where the section says something about the building itself - its storeys and material, its name, its use (hotel, lodging house, apartment house, hall, institution), a firm that occupied it, a construction, or a sale with its form and price. Left out at extraction: sellers, buyers, lessors and lessees who are private people, estates named for them, and a savings bank's printed list of depositors.

coverage.remaining: The rest of the 1911 paper - 8,897 OCR pages outside the real-estate section, where fires, building permits and news reports sit - is on disk but unread for this batch. 1912 (2,680 pages already extracted from curiv_angwin_ver02; calipatria_ver03 and dardanelle_ver01 not yet fetched) and 1913 (curiv_grimes_ver01) are the next years of the same section.
coverage.note: 633 numbered-address mentions on the 96 section pages. A rough automated split puts about 290 of them beside an advertiser's or a firm's own name - real-estate offices, land companies, steamship agencies advertising where to call - and about 16 in a savings bank's printed list of named depositors, which is never taken; about 10 are outside the city. The remaining ~320 were read one by one. Not taken from them: bare leases of a store or building that say nothing about it and name no firm (about 60), meetings held at what reads as a private house, police items naming householders, and numbers the OCR destroyed. 135 findings, 5 of them buildings the section names or credits without a street number.
